newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FORECAST-S.Africa's Citadel sees rate cut in Q2 97.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-S.Africa's Citadel sees rate cut in Q2 97.

text.p: South African interest rates were only likely to enter a downward phase in the second quarter of 1997, Citadel Investment Services said on Thursday.
Citadel was formerly known as JMM Investment Services.

Outlining investment prospects for 1997, the portfolio management company said that for interest rates to begin declining, the country's balance of payments situation had to improve, while high consumer borrowing would also have to show signs of abating.

South Africa's current account deficit was running at 4.6 billion rand in the second quarter of 1996, while private sector credit extension was running at 350 billion rand in August, according to latest available statistics.
These two factors were only likely to begin showing signs of improvement towards the end of the first quarter of next year.
"We will, therefore, not be surprised if the first signs of a downward phase in interest rates only commences somewhere in the second quarter of 1997," it said.
South African interest rates have been in an upward phase since September 1994.
As declining interest rates were also accompanied by a downturn in the country's economic activity, this would lead to weaker company profits.
This implied that before lower interest rates could benefit the local stock market in the coming year, share prices should ideally first react to weaker profit prospects.
"We consequently doubt if share prices will show any significant upward movement in the coming six months," it said.

A large uncertainty in the coming year would be the performance of the U.S. stock market. Corrections on the American bourse had always affected local share prices, despite the fact that South African shares might have been more realistically priced, Citadel said.
"Therefore, despite prospects of a lowering of interest rates in the year to come, this risk dare not be underestimated," it said.
It said that while the rand was unlikely to strengthen before the balance of payments and money supply growth improved, the probability of a further significant depreciation was limited.
The rand has lost more than 25 percent of its value against the dollar since February 15 this year.
Citadel cautioned investors to be wary of making assumptions about the rand's performance in the coming year on the grounds of the past year's performance.

JMM Investment Services announced on Thursday it had changed its name to Citadel. The independent portfolio manager, which focuses on the high income bracket of the market, has funds under supervision of about 700 million rand.
